summary.intent: Ship two GSD milestone-v2.0 phases (74: Rust/FUSE rotation-revocation soundness, 75: cross-language IPNS/node-codec verification parity) through the full autonomous ship-phase pipeline (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR/resolve-reviews/learnings), and specifically root-cause and fix a macOS-only Desktop-E2E failure blocking PR #607 before merge.
summary.outcome: PR #607 (Phase 74) was fixed with two real bugs found via local FUSE-T reproduction — a scope-exit rotation stale-refresh key clobber and an access-token TTL too short for the macOS E2E run — verified 3/3 green on CI across macOS/Windows/Linux, and merged to main; Phase 75 was then rebased onto main and taken partway through its own ship-phase flow (parity fixes for hex/base64 and CBOR edge cases applied and tested, CodeRabbit review in progress) when the transcript ends.

repo: FUSE-T's overwrite-rename on macOS opens the SOURCE file (not just the destination) mid-rename; Linux's kernel rename never opens either file. This is why identical rotation/e2e tests pass on Linux/Windows and fail deterministically on macOS.

A stale in-flight FUSE metadata refresh (apply_owned_children) can clobber a just-rotated inode's read_key back to its pre-rotation value if the rotated folder isn't marked in mutated_folders — the existing drain_refresh_completions guard (mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved) only protects folders already tracked as locally mutated.

GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' as a phase plan (e.g. a file named *-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md), producing false 'Executing' dashboard status for fully complete phases.

Two legitimate but indistinguishable-at-type-level wire encoding domains exist in CipherBox: internal node-codec fields (readKeySealed, read_sealed) use base64; share API wire fields (encryptedReadKey, encryptedWriteKey, itemNameEncrypted) use hex, enforced by API DTO @Matches regex. Nothing currently forces call sites to pick the right one, causing recurring hex/base64 bugs.

apps/api access token TTL is hardcoded 15m; the desktop test-login flow authenticates once at startup with no auto-refresh-on-401, so long-running headless E2E sessions (macOS legs with extra 120s+300s sync waits) can 401-lock mid-suite.

Rust rotation engine republishes read-key-rotated nodes with write_sealed: None (deferred to a later phase), which causes background owned-walks to fail with 'no write_sealed body' and, more seriously, means replay.rs cannot recover the signing seed after rotation — a real durability gap distinct from the Part D crypto race.

write_sealed AAD binds node.generation(), so after a rotation bumps generation, any preserved write body must be re-sealed at the new generation with the (stable) write key — it cannot just be carried forward unchanged.

Building the fuse/desktop crates on this macOS host links against macFUSE's fuse.pc by default; reproducing real FUSE-T/SMB behavior requires overriding PKG_CONFIG_PATH with a FUSE-T-aliased fuse.pc and confirming @rpath/libfuse-t.dylib linkage.

IPNS resolveRecord in apps/api is DB-preferred (read-after-write consistent) for normal rows; only a seqFloor branch for shared-folder edge cases serves network/DHT data with lag — confirmed via instrumentation showing 596 normal / 0 seqFloor resolves in a full test run.

code.finding: rotate_read_on_scope_exit fix: after refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys, mark all rotated folder inos into fs.mutated_folders so a stale concurrent metadata refresh uses mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved (preserves keys) instead of apply_owned_children (clobbers keys) — root fix for the macOS-only Part D overwrite-rename AES-GCM/EACCES failure.

re_mint_grants_rooted_at was base64-encoding the share grant's encryptedReadKey but all 4 share API DTOs (create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) validate it as hex — caused SC#2 grant re-mint to 400 at runtime on the FUSE→API round-trip, invisible to mocked unit tests.
ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL hardcoded to 15m; made env-configurable (default unchanged) so the desktop-e2e stack can raise it to 2h for long headless macOS runs without touching production.

apply_owned_children's File arm unconditionally re-materializes children with cid: String::new() and a freshly-derived read_key, discarding any locally-refreshed state — the mechanism that clobbers rotated keys when called on a stale refresh.

resolveRecord's seqFloor branch for shared-folder nodes serves the network/someguy record (DHT-lag ~10-30s) rather than the DB; ruled out as the Part D cause via instrumentation but is a real latent inconsistency worth knowing about.

workflow: When a background sub-agent's initial hand-off summary claims more progress than actually landed (e.g. 'spawning planner' vs 7 draft plans already on disk), always verify against disk state (git log, ls PLAN files, frontmatter) rather than trusting the notification text.

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree — the working pattern for resuming background planning after a quota reset is sequential processing on the main checkout, switching branches per phase, not worktree isolation.

When a user challenges a diagnosis with concrete log evidence, drop the hypothesis immediately and re-derive from the evidence rather than defending the prior read — the user's FUSE-T/macOS-only framing here was correct and the initial '401 infra flake' framing was wrong.

For hard-to-reproduce CI-only failures, locally reproducing the exact CI environment (same binary flags, same FUSE-T linkage, same fresh docker/DB/kubo reset) is dramatically faster for root-causing than iterating via CI dispatch — each local iteration was ~10 min vs ~30-40 min for a full CI round-trip.

Targeted temporary debug logging (single-line key/state fingerprints at decision points) resolved an intermittent-looking race far faster than theorizing from code reading alone; revert the instrumentation once the mechanism is confirmed, then implement the real fix.
Before implementing a systemic refactor (e.g. branded encoding types), capture it as a well-specified todo and defer — don't let a genuine hardening need block or bloat the PR that surfaced it.

GSD's todo auto-close on phase completion can under-close: todos tagged resolves_phase:N can be genuinely resolved by shipped code but stay stranded in pending/ — worth auditing pending todos against merged code+tests when picking up a new phase.

Rebasing a background-planned branch onto a newly-merged main can hit STATE.md/ROADMAP.md conflicts from concurrent phase bookkeeping churn; safe resolution is to prefer the phase branch's version for these files since the ship flow regenerates them anyway.

friction: Repeatedly mischaracterized the macOS Desktop-E2E failure as a '401 infra flake' before the user pushed back with concrete log evidence, requiring a full re-diagnosis.

Six failed root-cause attempts (write_sealed preservation, FilePointer self-heal x2, coalesced dest-gate, revert-and-retry cycles) before finding the actual fix (mark rotated folders as mutated) — each requiring a full local rebuild+reset+run cycle (~10 min).

Local reproduction required a fragile multi-step environment setup (FUSE-T vs macFUSE linking gotcha, stale go-nfsv4 mount processes, full 3-layer docker/DB/kubo reset needed for determinism since partial resets desync sequences).

A newly-surfaced Greptile P1 finding arrived mid-flow on Windows-only code (#[cfg(windows)]) that couldn't be compiled or tested locally on macOS, forcing a port-by-inspection fix verified only by CI.
API response stalled mid-stream twice during long agentic sequences, requiring the user to nudge continuation.
Sub-agent worktree isolation for background planning failed outright (EnterWorktree cannot pin into existing worktrees from repo root), wasting a planning cycle and requiring a pivot mid-session.
GSD commit helper intermittently false-negatives commit_failed while the commit actually lands, requiring manual git log verification before retrying.

Session quota limits interrupted the autonomous multi-phase pipeline three times, requiring cron-based scheduled resumes with corrected instructions each time as the working method (sequential-on-main, no worktrees) was discovered.
open_items: Hex/base64 wire-encoding domain hardening (authoritative doc, named boundary codecs, branded types, contract test, comment reconciliation) — captured as high-severity todo, deferred to a future phase.
rotation republish drops write_sealed body (durability bug: owned-walks fail post-rotation, replay.rs can't recover signing seed) — todo filed, not fixed in PR #607.
Desktop Rust client has no auto-refresh-on-401 (product-side gap; webview mitigates in production but headless/background sessions could 401-lock) — todo filed.

ts-rotatednodes-defensive-copy-parity — TS rotatedNodes map stores key references (not clones like Rust) for the root/child commit branches; only the repairDirtyNode site got a defensive copy — todo remains open.
re-mint trusts server for recipient-pubkey binding (inherited MEDIUM crypto finding, newly reachable on desktop) — todo logged, not fixed.

macOS/FUSE-T SMB client cache doesn't revalidate on remote changes (tests 5 & 7 in desktop-e2e permanently gated optional-on-macOS, related to existing #560 stopgap) — explicitly out of scope, unrelated to the Part D fix.
ts-validitytype-float-vs-integer CBOR parity (benign-direction finding from phase-75 crypto review) — todo filed instead of fixed.
Phases 76, 78, 79 remain fully unplanned/unstarted, on hold since the user paused the autonomous cascade.

Phase 75 ship-phase flow was mid-CodeRabbit-review when the transcript ends — SDK E2E gate passed, parity fixes committed, but Steps 6-11 (CodeRabbit triage, ship/PR, resolve reviews, learnings) not yet complete.
